The characters' dynamics in the provided text highlight the central themes of illusion versus reality and the corruption of the American Dream. Jay Gatsby’s relentless pursuit of Daisy Buchanan serves as the primary vehicle for exploring these themes. Gatsby’s idealization of Daisy represents the "illusion" aspect, where he projects his hopes and the attainability of the American Dream onto a person who is, in reality, shallow and bound by societal barriers. This dynamic underscores the hollowness of materialistic values, as Gatsby’s tragic downfall results from his inability to distinguish between his constructed fantasy and the actual nature of Daisy and the society she represents. The tension between Gatsby’s unwavering belief and the insurmountable reality of class and social structure emphasizes the futility of his quest, thereby critiquing the era's values.
